$comment: Accepted-problem baseline for scripts/check-railway-deploy-drift.mjs.
The drift check fails on any service that is not running everything that can
reach it and is NOT listed here. An entry means: this service is knowingly
behind, it has an owner issue, and it must not page again until that issue moves.
Entries are matched on service:verdict exactly, and the split is the same one
scripts/check-seed-freshness.mjs applies to compact health -- same function, so
expiry and prune-on-recovery cannot drift into two different meanings.
A service that recovers is reported as 'recovered' on the next run (prune it).
A service that fails with a DIFFERENT verdict than the one baselined blocks,
which is the point: BEHIND on a service baselined for REJECTED_PUSH is a new
failure wearing an old name.
This file held 62 REJECTED_PUSH entries -- every service carrying a Railway
watch-path filter -- until #6142. They were not degradations: the check demanded
that a FILTERED service run HEAD, which under a watch-path filter is not the
healthy state. Re-measured across the fleet, 7,331 of 7,391 path-reason skips
were plainly correct and the other 60 are explained (build context, and a
registry closure not yet applied to Railway). The check is now closure-aware and
reports CURRENT_FOR_CLOSURE for those services instead, so the entries are gone
rather than suppressed. Do not re-add them: a REJECTED_PUSH today means Railway
refused a push that DID reach the service, which is a real failure.
expiresAt forces a re-review of the whole file. A stale-deploy suppression that
outlives its cause is how a fleet ends up silently a week behind. It does not fire
on an EMPTY list -- with nothing suppressed there is nothing to re-review, and a
red monitor with no finding behind it is how people learn to ignore this check.
The list is empty as of 2026-08-06. It held one entry: `umami` at BEHIND against
#6064, the GitHub integration that stopped delivering pushes to the analytics
collector. The check reported it `recovered` once umami was running head again,
and the reconciler in .github/workflows/railway-deploy-trigger.yml is now what
keeps it there -- it judges each service against the commit it is RUNNING, so a
webhook that goes quiet again self-heals on the next reconcile instead of needing
an entry here.
2026-08-12: this file briefly held 31 REJECTED_PUSH entries against #6378
while Railway wait-for-CI refusals (the 2026-08-07..12 deploy-gate outage,
fixed by #6513, plus the c001e7566 history reset) kept the reconciler-less
fleet knowingly behind. The fleet converged the same day and every entry
cleared on the next live run, so the list is empty again. The episode
hardened the mechanism, and those properties remain: an entry may pin a
rejectedShas cohort (a rejection carrying any SHA outside it blocks, so a
recovered service's NEXT rejection cannot inherit an old suppression);
REJECTED_PUSH with an unidentified running source is a separate
undeterminable verdict this file cannot acknowledge at all; entry-level
expiry re-pages WITH attribution (expiredEntry + issue on the blocking
item); and multi-entry cohorts should stagger expiries so a re-page is a
reviewable trickle, not a wall.
